description: Add a 3D file viewer to the HelpingHands iOS and macOS apps so the SO-101 gripper designs (Blender/OpenSCAD/Build123d outputs in cad/) can be viewed in-app. Support viewing any 3D file the bake-off produces (e.g. STL/OBJ/STEP/USDC as applicable); simple viewer screen reachable from the app, loading files from the repo bundle or imported files.

results.identified_issue:
The repo had only an iOS target; the pebble says "iOS and macOS apps", so I added a HelpingHandsMac target in project.yml sharing HelpingHands/ + Generated/ sources with its own generated Info-macOS.plist (the iOS one carries UILaunchScreen/orientation keys and xcodegen would clash writing one path from two targets). I deliberately left ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME off the Mac target: Assets.xcassets only has an iOS AppIcon idiom and actool fails a macOS build when it can't find a matching set. Risk is contained — xcodebuild builds one scheme, so a broken Mac target cannot break Vigil's iOS builds. I typechecked every new file with swiftc against both the iphoneos and macosx SDKs (clean) and ran the STL parser for real on macOS against all nine exports, but did NOT run a full xcodebuild (the skill forbids building), so PebblesKit compiling for macOS is unverified — it declares .macOS(.v14) and PebblesBannerView has macOS branches, so it should be fine.

STL parsing: format detection is by length arithmetic (84 + 50*n), NOT the "solid" prefix — OpenSCAD writes "OpenSCAD..." and build123d writes "STL Exported..." into the 80-byte BINARY header, so a prefix sniff would misroute both to the ASCII path. Facet normals that are zero or non-finite are recomputed from the cross product (Blender's exports rely on this). Vertices are not welded (STL has no shared-vertex table), giving flat shading, which is what you want for CAD. CAD exports are Z-up and SceneKit is Y-up, so the pivot node is rotated -pi/2 about X.

Camera: SceneView's allowsCameraControl mutates the pointOfView node in place, so "reset view" works by bumping a generation counter that rebuilds the camera node and the SceneView's .id. If framing looks wrong for a much larger or smaller part, the distance formula is radius / tan(fov/2) * 1.5 in ModelSceneView.makeCamera().

Staging: Scripts/stage_cad_models.py runs as a postBuildScript, which is after the resources phase but still before codesign, so writing into $BUILT_PRODUCTS_DIR/$UNLOCALIZED_RESOURCES_FOLDER_PATH is safe. I chose this over committing copies of the 7.8 MB of STL into the source tree or over XcodeGen folder references (three source dirs named export/out would collide in the bundle). STEP payloads are NOT copied — only their parsed header goes in manifest.json — which keeps ~8 MB of unrenderable B-rep out of the app. If the human later wants STEP to render, the only real option is tessellating it server-side or at build time into STL/USD; there is no on-device path.
results.summary: Added a 3D file viewer that opens every STL the gripper bake-off produced, on iPhone and on a new Mac target.
results.detailed_description:
There's a new "Gripper CAD" card on the home screen. It lists all nine STLs from the OpenSCAD, Blender and build123d bake-off, grouped by engine, and opens each one in a SceneKit viewport you can orbit, pinch and pan. Under the model it shows the bounding box in millimetres, the triangle count and the file size, so you can compare the three engines' output directly. Toolbar buttons toggle wireframe, spin and reset-view. There's also an Import button for any STL, OBJ, PLY or USD file on your device.

Two things to know about how it's built. SceneKit has no STL importer, so I wrote the binary and ASCII STL reader myself — I ran it over all nine exports and it reads them correctly (the gripper measures 65.2 × 52.0 × 105.4 mm, 5,966 to 34,903 triangles depending on the engine). And STEP genuinely can't be rendered on iOS or macOS — that needs a CAD kernel — so the STEP files are listed with their header info (tool, date, schema) and a note saying why, rather than silently missing.

The meshes are copied into the app bundle by a build phase reading cad/ directly, so rebuilding the gripper is enough to update the app. I also added a HelpingHandsMac target and wired PB_MACOS_SCHEME, since there was no macOS app before — I type-checked everything against both SDKs but I did not compile the Mac target end to end, so that's the piece to try first with ./build_macos.sh --local.
